components.notes: Already encoded, externally driven scalar launch source. Fixed source/encoding overhead is illustrative. The source input interface is outside this distribution subcircuit; this does not implement a neural operation.
Fixed 50:50 two-way splitter; 0.2 dB is excess insertion loss in addition to division. No continuously tunable splitting or lossless duplication.
Uniform, matched, single-mode waveguide with constant coefficients inside the declared envelope. Width times length estimates occupied core area, excluding spacing and bends.

Ideal calibrated normalized sample output plus shot and input-referred electronic noise. Minimum power is minimum full-scale calibration power, not a requirement that x=0 emit light. One electrical load only; cost assumes receiver and normalization electronics.

Ideal linear intensity reencoder: output full scale is carrier power times insertion transmission. The carrier and one normalized electrical sample must both be supplied. Drive/normalization overhead is included only as an illustrative fixed cost.

assumptions: One scalar, nonnegative intensity sample, x in [0,1], per optical lane and rectangular symbol; negative signed NN values need a separately specified encoder.
Full-scale power is a calibration/operating-point parameter. Energy is a full-scale-per-symbol upper bound, not workload-averaged energy.
Passive components are matched, reflection-free, single-mode and linear; parameters are constant only within the stated envelope.
Receiver gain and modulation are ideally calibrated. Detector quantum efficiency thins a Poisson photon count; a separate input-referred RMS term models electronics.
Physical ports allow one connection each, including electrical outputs; electrical broadcast needs additional modeled components.
Electrical receiver/reencoder fixed costs are illustrative lumped overheads; no free detector or carrier source is implied.
excluded_effects: Fabrication/layout/DRC and foundry qualification
Signed, coherent, phase, wavelength-multiplexed or quantum state encoding
Back reflections, interference, dispersion, crosstalk, bends and coupling/packaging loss
Bandwidth waveform distortion, modulator extinction/nonlinearity and laser start-up dynamics
Temperature variation within the envelope, process variation, ageing and calibration drift
NN task accuracy, covariance guarantees after regeneration, complete memory/control/IO costs
Optical amplification, serialized delivery, switching and storage

scope.implementation: one NN node's scalar-lane optical fanout distribution subcircuit
scope.encoding: normalized intensity P=P_full_scale*x, nominal 0<=x<=1; no implicit rescaling
scope.input_boundary: each encoded_launch source is externally driven by the selected NN value; NN computation and encoding/driver internals are outside this subcircuit
scope.output_boundary: complete calibrated electrical samples at receiver ports; wiring and consumer NN operators are outside this subcircuit
scope.energy: full-scale per-symbol electrical energy upper bound under the declared nominal model; includes every launch and carrier source and component overhead; not workload averaged
scope.latency: complete-symbol readiness from launch start; one acquisition interval at launch and an additional interval for each regeneration; fixed component overheads are additional
scope.carrier_schedule: fresh carrier for each generated regenerative branch is gated to one symbol at reencoding; startup/transient and standby costs are excluded
scope.noise: first-order normalized full-scale covariance and RMS estimate with shared upstream contributions; not a guaranteed NN error bound, clipping proof, or task-accuracy prediction
scope.termination: unused optical leaves are ideal matched external termination boundaries; their power is lost and not redistributed; termination device area/cost is outside scope
scope.aggregation: subcircuit instance costs only; not added to legacy neural macro estimates

scope.locks: locks filter the submitted grid; they do not insert choices or silently change a candidate
scope.relaxations: single-constraint suggestions are witnessed by physically feasible evaluated candidates that fail exactly one declared numeric requirement; no global minimum relaxation is claimed
scope.evidence: model-based estimates using embedded technology assumptions; planning does not run external simulation or confer calibration
